prompt:
A densely annotated editorial infographic plate, drawn by hand in confident ink
line with light watercolour and gouache wash on bright warm-white paper.
Contour line varies in weight and is charcoal near-black. Dimensional but not
photographic: restrained hatching, subtle texture, believable volume, selective
shadow, clean uncluttered background. Every material reads as itself — dull grey
lead, unglazed earthenware, weathered timber, damp fibrous bark — and materials
that differ in the explanation look visibly different. Quiet palette of stone,
clay, wood, and metal tones over the warm-white ground, with one or two
desaturated accents that each keep a single meaning throughout the plate.
Contemporary editorial typography: one calm display face for the title, one
highly legible face for the many small labels, sentence case, crisply printed
and correctly spelled. Annotation is dense and disciplined — leader lines,
brackets, dimension marks, magnified inset circles, small side studies — laid
out so no two leaders cross. Asymmetric composition with about a quarter of the
page left quiet. Modern printing on clean stock: fresh, crisp, and unaged. The
only lettering anywhere on the plate is the title, the deck, the labels, and the
short notes. The words hero, drawing, figure, plate, inset, zone, band, strip,
trio, column, and cutaway describe the construction of the page and are never
lettered onto it, alone or in a phrase: no headings that name parts of the
layout, no percentages or
proportions of the page, no tags in brackets after a label or note, no sentence
describing the drawing or explaining what the reader is meant to see, no
signature, monogram, date, watermark, or credit line.

The plate is headed "acrylic", with the standing line "A desktop workbench that turns a reference photo into real acrylic paint choices, mixing recipes, and a shopping list." beneath it.

The dominant picture, filling roughly half the page, shows A photograph resting on a drop zone at upper left; arrows carry it rightward into a small clustering diagram where scattered pixel dots collapse into ten flat swatches stacked by pixel count; each swatch then sends a line into a catalog of paint tubes, where one swatch resolves into two tubes squeezed side by side onto a proportional mixing bar. One arrow returns leftward from a slider back to the clustering diagram, showing reprocessing.

Magnified circles set beside it show A circle over the clustering diagram, showing pixel dots pulled toward centroids. A circle over one paint tube label, showing brand, series, pigment code. A circle over the mixing bar, showing a 2:3 ratio split and the resulting mixed swatch beside the target swatch.

Colour is used so that One warm accent marks the source image and its extracted colours. One cool accent marks catalogued paints and their matches. A muted grey marks paints already owned; the warm accent marks paints that must be bought.

Draw these quantities as dimension marks or counts: 10 dominant colors by default, adjustable from 2 to 40. 3 ranked single-paint matches kept per color. 117 Golden paints seeded on first launch. Image resized to 256 by 256 before extraction. Thumbnails 80 by 80.

These trade words appear on the plate, each set against the thing it names: nColors on the slider; K-Means on the clustering diagram; delta E and CIEDE2000 on the comparison arc; parts on the mixing bar ratio; owned on the greyed tubes; posterize, tile size, smoothing, aspect ratio on the canvas controls; Comparison, Shopping List, Color Detail, Paint by Numbers on the four exported pages; favorites on the saved recipe card; acrylic.db, state.json, projects, thumb on the stored files.

Letter these words onto the drawings, spelled exactly as given: drop image, paste image, K-Means, dominant colors, nColors 2-40, paint catalog, CIEDE2000, delta E, mixing recipe, parts ratio, reprocess; pixel count, Lab values, opacity, target vs mix; posterize, tile size, smoothing, aspect ratio, owned only; Comparison, Shopping List, Color Detail, Paint by Numbers, favorites; acrylic.db, projects, thumb, state.json

Set these short notes beside what they explain: Clustering seeded for repeatable palettes; Recipes search two-paint mixes, then three; Single paint wins if closer. Ratings run Perfect to Approximate. Owned only matches your existing tubes. Shopping list lists unowned paints only; Paint by numbers is a placeholder page. Deleting a project removes its folder.
